editorial.headline: Where ‘Other New Goods’ Meets Bali’s PMA Barrier
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 47799 covers specialised retail of new goods not otherwise classified, nationally open to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47799 is a deliberately broad retail category: specialised sales of new goods that are not classified elsewhere. Its scope includes cleaning materials, bamboo, sandalwood, damar resin, weapons and ammunition. That range is the point. The activity is defined not by one product line or a single kind of shop, but by the retail sale of particular new goods that sit outside more specifically described activity categories. It is a classification for businesses whose merchandise may be highly varied, while remaining within specialised retail.

The registration picture is broad at the business-scale level. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In practical terms, the national record does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. That national openness is an important part of the classification’s commercial reading, but it is not the whole Indonesian picture for a founder choosing Bali as the place of PMA registration.

In Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity through PMA today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO: at the Besar scale, every scope is assessed as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, placing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The record identifies this restriction as taking effect through the Bali moratorium of May 2026. The national ceiling of 100% therefore remains a national position, while Bali’s PMA registration outcome is blocked.

That distinction deserves to be read plainly. A founder can accurately see an activity that is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, across every listed business scale, and still face a complete Bali-specific PMA registration barrier. For this code, the decisive Bali issue is not the nature of bamboo, cleaning materials, sandalwood, resin, weapons or ammunition as individual products. It is the activity’s risk treatment at the Besar scale and the province’s stated moratorium rule. The classification is nationally open; Bali’s PMA door is closed.
editorial.pullQuote: The classification is nationally open; Bali’s PMA door is closed.
